==English== ===Alternative forms=== * {{alt|en|extream|extreame||obsolete}} * {{alt|en|xtreme||informal|nonstandard}} ===Etymology=== Borrowed into late {{inh|en|enm|-}} from {{der|en|fro|extreme}}, from {{der|en|la|extrēmus}}, the superlative of {{m|la|exter}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/ɪkˈstɹiːm/|/ɛkˈstɹiːm/|a=RP}} * {{IPA|en|/ɪkˈstɹim/|/ɛkˈstɹim/|a=GA}} ** {{audio|en|En-us-extreme.ogg|a=California}} * {{rhymes|en|iːm|s=2}} ===Adjective=== {{wikidata lexeme|L6521}} {{en-adj|er,more}} # Of a place, the most [[remote]], [[farthest]] or [[outermost]]. #: {{syn|en|farthest|furthest|most [[distant]]|outermost|remotest}} #: {{ant|en|closest|nearest}} #: {{ux|en|At the '''extreme''' edges, the coating is very thin.}} # In the [[greatest]] or [[highest]] [[degree]]; [[intense]]. #: {{syn|en|greatest|highest|dreadful|Thesaurus:extreme}} #: {{ant|en|least}} #: {{ux|en|He has an '''extreme''' aversion to needles, and avoids visiting the doctor.}} #* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=13|passage=And Vickers launched forth into a tirade very different from his platform utterances. He said that if you wanted to do anything for them, you must rule them, not pamper them.}} #* {{RQ:en:CNN|author=Reuters|title=Chipmakers look to Japan as worries about China grow|url=https://www.cnn.com/2023/05/18/tech/chipmaking-japan-china-g7|date=2023-05-18|passage=Micron said in a statement that it would bring '''extreme''' ultraviolet (EUV) technology to Japan, becoming the first semiconductor company to do so, and expected to invest up to 500 billion yen ($3.6 billion) with support from the Japanese government.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20251118173332/https://www.cnn.com/2023/05/18/tech/chipmaking-japan-china-g7|archivedate=18 November 2025}} # {{U|excessive}}, or [[far]] [[beyond]] the [[norm]]. #: {{syn|en|immoderate|unrestrained|Thesaurus:excessive}} #: {{ant|en|moderate|reasonable}} #: {{ux|en|His '''extreme''' love of model trains showed in the rails that criscrossed his entire home.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|date=2013-03 |author=Frank Fish; George Lauder|volume=101|issue=2|page=114|magazine=w:American Scientist |title=[http://www.americanscientist.org/issues/feature/2013/2/not-just-going-with-the-flow Not Just Going with the Flow] |passage=An '''extreme''' version of vorticity is a ''vortex''. Make me the gaſtly counterfeit of death.}} # {{lb|en|mathematics}} Either of the two numbers at the ends of a [[proportion]], as ''1'' and ''6'' in ''1:2=3:6''. ====Translations==== {{trans-top|greatest or utmost point, degree or condition}} * Bulgarian: * Catalan: * Chinese: * Danish: * Dutch: * Esperanto: * Finnish: * French: * German: * Greek: * Italian: * Japanese: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Swedish: * Tagalog: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|each of the things at opposite ends of a range or scale}} * Catalan: * Czech: * Dutch: * Esperanto: * Finnish: * French: * Hungarian: * Irish: * Italian: * Japanese: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Swedish: * Tagalog: * Welsh: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|drastic expedient}} * Azerbaijani: * Finnish: * French: * Polish: * Russian: {{t+|ru|кра́йность}} {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|either of the two numbers at the ends of a proportion}} * Finnish: * Tagalog: {{trans-bottom}} ===Adverb=== {{en-adv}} # {{lb|en|archaic}} [[extremely|Extremely]]. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1796|author=Charles Burney|title=Memoirs of the Life and Writings of Metastasio|section=2.5 |passage=''In the empty and '''extreme''' cold theatre.''}} ====Usage notes==== * Formerly used to modify adjectives and sometimes adverbs, but rarely verbs. ====Derived terms==== {{col|en |extremism |extremist |extremity |extremely |extreme ironing |extreme unction }} ===Related terms=== * {{l|en|extremum}} ===See also=== * {{l|en|mean}} ===References=== * {{R:OED2}}
